method: Complete source reading and paragraph-aligned English restoration, followed by a source/translation reread and targeted saved-file checks of the argument-sensitive passages. Not represented as independent review.

findings: Restored all 42 source paragraphs instead of the previous 15 paragraphs plus six invented section headings.
Restored the reverse-direction compulsory return to the cave, the offense/wrong-outsider qualification, practical examples and the shared landing point not being corroboration.
Corrected the former ending which assigned the harder story to Plato; the source calls the SAE story harder than getting out.
anchors: Same cut produces real gain and the unseen simultaneously, not a discovery delayed until later.
Prisoners possess real predictive ability; mistaking the gain for the whole is the error.
Outside questioning is useful through noncoincidence, not an authority that guarantees correctness.
The remainder permits another cut but commands none; contingent initiative identifies whose act, not why it occurs.
Socrates withholds a guarantee for his interpretation, not for the stability of the image.

independent_review_corrections.issue: Restored the declarative still a cave rather than the old alternative-question wording.

independent_review_corrections.before: That sentence clarifies whose event this is, not why it happens. Nor is the gap a temporary oversight. SAE has been dismantling engines all along: attraction, necessity, every cannot-not. By the end it has no engine of its own left either. It can say what happens after a cut is made. It cannot say why a person makes the cut.
independent_review_corrections.after: That sentence clarifies whose event this is, not why it happens. Nor is the gap a temporary oversight. independent_review_corrections.issue: Removed added universal every cannot-not, which could erase the subject’s own cannot-not.

findings: Restored the complete 48-paragraph progression rather than 17 paragraphs under five added section headings.
Restored the parent-and-child example and the pressure inherent in leaving an empty foundation slot.
Removed the former addition about the sun sustaining generation and growth: a Platonic claim, but not present in this essay’s Chinese passage.
anchors: Cannot explain today is distinct from in-principle unsayability; the principal is never repaid in the book.
A source can be worshipped, an operation only used; unavoidable does not mean generative.
Good is content-bearing and gives direction and worth, not an empty metaphysical label.
The exemption is the remainder of examination, not an honor or privilege.
Undeniability states status, not productivity; the counterquestion remains unanswered.

findings: Restored all 48 source paragraphs, including the complete wardrobe example and the repeated qualification that unequal divisions reveal but do not originate the ranking.
Removed the added final system-level trade-off paragraph and the invented claim that rank is useful because it is easier to administer.
Restored Plato’s distinct first and second counterquestions rather than condensing them into one general objection.
Batch reread: retained the source’s definite loss-of-visibility claim after ranking rather than weakening it to harder to see.
anchors: The third/fourth division concerns treatment of the starting point, not objects.
The unequal ratio is the earliest appearance of hierarchy, not its source; equal divisions would not remove Plato’s ranking.
Four liabilities are horizontal, neither exhaustive nor mutually exclusive.
Debt stays recorded even when it cannot be discharged in the original ledger.
The feeling of ascent is a real acquisition; translating it into height exceeds its warrant.
The ladder retains practical educational force that the ledger does not claim to replace.

findings: Restored all45 source paragraphs, including the bronze horse and accidental ring turn, Gyges’s ancestor qualification, the clean extreme comparison, and all three counterquestions.
Removed an added paragraph offering a structural-loss answer on SAE’s behalf where the source only leaves the challenge open.
Restored the forthcoming creditor at the book’s end and the explicit personal choice to accept or decline questioning.
anchors: Glaucon strengthens a position he does not endorse; the ring establishes a premise, not a proof from the shepherd’s eventual outcome.
What rolls is the lowered threshold, not an exponentially growing number of wrong acts.
The descent can feel genuinely like increasing competence.
Self-questioning is useful but cannot guarantee coverage of its blind spots.
The account is a bill, not a command; no outsider is granted authority to legislate for the subject.
Where the debt exists, whom the account helps, and how creditorless debt differs from a divine watcher remain live objections.

findings: Restored all48 paragraphs, including dyeing wool, the child with sweets, moderation crossing the table’s boxes, and Socrates’ prior warning that his method is a shortcut.
Removed invented examples of sleep, trauma and forgetting, and removed the added SAE claim about resisting an internal sovereign.
Restored the distinction of 16 finite but order-constitutive levels and the unresolved personal-continuity question.
anchors: The third part is established with Leontius’ story after the first two are separated by a rule.
A chain differs from a table by provenance and nonpermutable order, not infinite versus finite size.
Non-acceptance leaves the lower proposal active and available for resubmission; it does not suppress its sender.
Plato’s parts are contemporaneous and unity is his declared result; the chain’s continuity remains a question.
Leontius’ failure remains unembellished, not rewritten into an illustration of perfect harmony.

cross_article_findings: The former English keeps many conclusions but repeatedly compresses concrete scenes and adds section headings; the full edition restores the essay sequence.
Counterquestions are left open where the Chinese leaves them open. Explanatory paragraphs added on SAE’s behalf were not retained.
A possible further cut is not a command, a test exemption is not a privilege, and a felt gain is not a fixed height. These qualifications were checked across the five essays.
corrections: EP01 final comparison restored: SAE’s story is harder than getting out, not Plato’s story harder than SAE’s.
EP03 paragraph36: removed an unintended weakening of the statement about what ranking hides.
Independent review: EP01 title changed to Outside the Cave, Still a Cave, preserving the Chinese declarative claim.
